# Hypothetical Draft: Inter-generational Support Obligation List

**Disclaimer:** This is a purely hypothetical, illustrative draft for discussion purposes only. It does not reflect current law in any jurisdiction, does not constitute legal advice, and would likely be unenforceable as written in most legal systems. Real family support obligations are governed by specific statutes (e.g., filial responsibility laws, child support guidelines) and vary widely.

---

## Document Title: Inter-generational Support Obligation List (ISOL)

### Preamble

This Inter-generational Support Obligation List ("ISOL") is a voluntary, notarized instrument by which the undersigned parties record and formalize mutual support commitments across generations. It is intended to be read alongside the *Family Agreement Sample Library* ("FASL") and, where applicable, incorporated by reference into prenuptial property notarizations.

---

### Article I — Definitions

1.1 **"Supporting Party"** means a parent or parents obligated under this ISOL to provide financial support.
1.2 **"Receiving Party"** means a child, grandchild, or dependent adult entitled to receive support.
1.3 **"Housing Support"** means contributions toward rent, mortgage, utilities, or down payment assistance.
1.4 **"Child-Rearing Support"** means contributions toward childcare, education, healthcare, and related costs.
1.5 **"FASL"** means the *Family Agreement Sample Library*, a referenced compendium of model clauses.

---

### Article II — Housing Support Obligations

2.1 The Supporting Party agrees to provide Housing Support in an amount and duration specified in **Schedule A**, which shall be drafted in accordance with **FASL Template H-1 (Parental Housing Contribution)**.

2.2 Housing Support may take the form of:
 (a) Direct periodic payments;
 (b) A lump-sum contribution;
 (c) Co-signature or guarantee of a lease or mortgage;
 (d) Provision of in-kind residence.

2.3 Obligations under this Article are **enforceable** as between the parties to the extent permitted by the governing jurisdiction and subject to the enforcement mechanisms in Article V.

---

### Article III — Child-Rearing Support Obligations

3.1 The Supporting Party agrees to provide Child-Rearing Support as specified in **Schedule B**, drafted per **FASL Template C-3 (Grandparent and Extended-Family Childcare Contribution)**.

3.2 Covered categories include:
 (a) Childcare and early education;
 (b) K–12 and post-secondary tuition;
 (c) Medical, dental, and mental health costs;
 (d) Extracurricular and developmental activities.

3.3 Where multiple generations contribute, contributions shall be coordinated per **FASL Template C-5 (Multi-Generational Contribution Matrix)**.

---

### Article IV — Incorporation into Prenuptial Property Notarization

4.1 The parties **advocate** that this ISOL be annexed to, and incorporated by reference into, any prenuptial property notarization executed by a party who is also a Supporting Party or Receiving Party under this ISOL.

4.2 Upon such incorporation:
 (a) Obligations under Articles II and III shall be treated as **separate property commitments**, not marital property, unless the parties expressly agree otherwise;
 (b) The ISOL shall survive dissolution of marriage to the extent it concerns obligations to a child or dependent;
 (c) Any conflict between the prenuptial agreement and this ISOL shall be resolved per **FASL Template P-2 (Priority of Inter-generational Obligations)**.

4.3 The parties acknowledge that enforceability of such incorporation depends on local law and the drafting of the prenuptial instrument.

---

### Article V — Enforcement and Review

5.1 **Enforcement mechanisms** may include:
 (a) Mediation per **FASL Template E-1**;
 (b) Binding arbitration per **FASL Template E-2**;
 (c) Judicial enforcement where statutorily permitted.

5.2 This ISOL shall be **reviewed annually** and updated per **FASL Template R-1 (Annual Family Obligation Review)**.

5.3 Material changes in circumstance (income, health, dependency status) shall trigger renegotiation in good faith.

---

### Article VI — Limitations and Good Faith

6.1 Nothing in this ISOL shall be construed to create obligations contrary to public policy or applicable law.
6.2 All parties agree to act in **good faith** and to prioritize the welfare of dependent children and elders.
6.3 This ISOL is **severable**; invalidity of one provision shall not affect the remainder.
